mainTopic: Walking to set up an עירוב as forbidden preparation, רב יהודה's rules for עירוב on two holy days in a row, and whether the two days of ראש השנה may be treated as separate days
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבה. A ברייתא forbids strolling by the city gate on שבת in order to reach the bathhouse right after, so walking on יום טוב to set up an עירוב for the next day should be forbidden too. The גמרא answers that the bathhouse case is obvious to onlookers, but someone walking to make an עירוב just looks like a scholar lost in thought or a man searching for his donkey. Then, with the word גופא, the גמרא returns to רב יהודה's rules for two holy days in a row. You may repeat the same kind of עירוב, and you may switch from bread to feet, but you may not switch from feet to bread. שמואל adds that a bread עירוב for the second day must use the same bread. רב אשי supports this from a משנה, while the רבנן reply that the משנה is only giving good advice. A new משנה follows in which רבי יהודה treats the two days of ראש השנה separately: a different עירוב for each day, a tithing condition on a basket, and an egg laid on the first day eaten on the second. רבי דוסא בן הרכינס also words the prayer conditionally, and each time the חכמים disagree. The גמרא asks who these חכמים are, and רב answers רבי יוסי. A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי alone forbids two עירובין on ראש השנה, because late witnesses make both days holy, so the two days form one holiness.

steps.title: רבה would have retracted had he heard the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge: a ברייתא forbids strolling near the city gate on שבת in order to reach the bathhouse right after שבת, so רבה should have retracted his lenient ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The ברייתא says:] A person may not stroll at the entrance of the city so that he can go into the bathhouse right away [after שבת]. [Had רבה heard this,] he would have retracted!
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts in the middle of a challenge. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and claims that if רבה had known it, he would have taken back his ruling about walking on the first day to set up an עירוב for the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that even plain walking on a holy day is forbidden if its purpose is to prepare for after the day ends. Walking on the first day of יום טוב to make an עירוב for the second day looks like the same kind of preparation. So רבה's lenient ruling seems to clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: he will stroll or walk about
the entrance or gate of the city
bathhouse
he retracts, takes back his statement

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The words 'A person may not stroll' are the end of a quoted ברייתא, and 'he would have retracted' is the גמרא's claim about רבה. They are not a new ruling of their own.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְטַיֵּיל אָדָם עַל פֶּתַח מְדִינָה
phrases.english: A person may not stroll at the entrance of the city
phrases.notes: The end of the quoted ברייתא, which began on the previous amud

phrases.english: in order to enter the bathhouse immediately [after Shabbat],
[had Rabba heard this] he would have retracted!
phrases.notes: The punch line of the challenge against רבה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge against רבה that began on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling permitting a person to walk on the first day of יום טוב to set up an עירוב for the second day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids walking on a holy day for a purpose that comes after the day. Walking to set up an עירוב for the next day should count as the same forbidden preparation.

steps.title: רבה heard it and did not retract: the cases differ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. In the ברייתא the purpose of the walking is obvious, but with an עירוב it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. He heard it and did not retract. There, the matter is obvious. Here, the matter is not obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the claim that רבה would have changed his mind. It says he knew the ברייתא and still kept his ruling, because the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is whether people watching can see what the walking is for. Someone strolling by the city gate just before the end of שבת is clearly waiting for the bathhouse, so his preparation is visible. Someone walking to the edge of town to set up an עירוב gives no visible sign of why he is there.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so (a formula that rejects a suggestion)
he heard it, he knew of that source
the matter is evident or recognizable
there (the ברייתא case) / here (the עירוב case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: forbidden walking for preparation depends on whether the purpose is visible to others, not only on what the person intends inside.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
he heard it and did not retract.
There, the matter is evident;
phrases.notes: 'There' means strolling by the city gate or walking out to your field.

phrases.english: here, the matter is not evident.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means walking out to set up an עירוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, שְׁמִעַ לֵיהּ וְלָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge in step 1 by showing the two cases are different
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the ברייתא's case and the עירוב case, so רבה's ruling stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge ignored that the ברייתא's case has a visible purpose, while walking to set up an עירוב does not.

steps.title: Why walking to make an עירוב looks innocent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why nobody would suspect the walking is preparation. A scholar seems lost in thought, and an unlearned person seems to be searching for his donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is a Torah scholar, we say: his learning pulled him along. And if he is an unlearned person, we say: his donkey got lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim that the purpose of the walking is not visible. It gives everyday explanations that an onlooker would naturally assume.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever the walker is, people watching have an innocent explanation ready. A צורבא מרבנן might be so deep in a Torah topic that he wandered far without noticing. An עם הארץ might be looking for a lost animal. Since nobody would think 'he is preparing for tomorrow', the walking does not count as visible preparation.

keyTerms.meaning: a young Torah scholar
his learning drew him along (he was absorbed in Torah study)
an unlearned person
his donkey got lost

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's ruling stands. Walking on the first day to set up an עירוב for the second day is allowed, because onlookers cannot tell it is preparation. The ברייתא only forbids preparation whose purpose is visible.

phrases.english: If he is a Torah scholar,
we say: his learning drew him along.
And if he is an unlearned person,
we say: his donkey got lost [and he is searching for it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the עירוב case is 'not evident', as claimed in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction by visibility: onlookers would give the walking an innocent explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Walking to set up an עירוב is forbidden preparation, just like strolling to reach the bathhouse
steps.terutzMaskana: Walking for an עירוב is not recognizable as preparation, so it is allowed and רבה did not retract

steps.title: רב יהודה: use the same type of עירוב on both days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now looks at רב יהודה's statement on its own. If you made an עירוב by feet for the first day, you make it by feet for the second. If you made it with bread for the first day, you make it with bread for the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the statement itself: רב יהודה said: If he made an עירוב with his feet on the first day, he makes an עירוב with his feet on the second. If he made an עירוב with bread on the first day, he makes an עירוב with bread on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to a statement it quoted earlier, רב יהודה's, to study it on its own. This step states his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב תחומין can be made in two ways: by being at the spot in person (by feet) or by placing bread there. רב יהודה says that on two days in a row, the method used for the first day may be used again for the second. The rule keeps the two days consistent, and the גמרא will now go on to discuss it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier
he made an עירוב with his feet (by being at the spot in person)
he made an עירוב with bread placed at the spot
the first day / the second day (of two holy days in a row)

steps.confusionAlert: גופא does not start a new topic from nowhere. It sends you back to a statement the גמרא already quoted in passing earlier, now to be analyzed in full.

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rav Yehuda said:
If he established an eiruv with his feet on the first day,
he establishes an eiruv with his feet on the second.
If he established an eiruv with bread on the first day,
he establishes an eiruv with bread on the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבה discussion and goes back to examine רב יהודה's statement, which was quoted earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On two holy days in a row, the method of עירוב used for the first day (by feet or with bread) may be used again for the second day.

steps.title: Switching from bread to feet is allowed, but not from feet to bread
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's statement continues. If you used bread for the first day, you may use your feet for the second. If you used your feet for the first day, you may not switch to bread for the second, because you may not start a bread עירוב on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made an עירוב with bread for the first day, he may make an עירוב with his feet for the second day. If he made an עירוב with his feet for the first day, he may not make an עירוב with bread for the second day, because one may not start a bread עירוב from scratch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of rules from רב יהודה that began in step 4. It now covers the two cases where a person switches from one type of עירוב to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירוב for the second day must be set up on the first day, which is itself holy. Setting out bread for the first time on a holy day looks like preparing one holy day for the next, and that is forbidden. Standing in place with your feet does not look like preparation (as step 3 explained), so switching to feet is fine, but switching to bread is not.

keyTerms.meaning: An עירוב made by placing bread (food) at a spot, making that spot your 'home' for שבת or יום טוב
An עירוב made 'with one's feet', by going and standing at the spot at nightfall
From the start; for the first time
Preparing on one holy day for the next, which is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: 'On the second day' means the עירוב that works for the second day. That עירוב is set up at the end of the first day, while it is still holy. This is why making a new bread עירוב is a problem.

phrases.english: If he made an eruv with bread for the first day —
he may make an eruv with his feet for the second.
phrases.notes: For example, if his bread was eaten.

phrases.english: If he made an eruv with his feet for the first day —
he may not make an eruv with bread for the second,
because one may not begin an eruv with bread from scratch.
phrases.notes: On a holy day, for the sake of the next holy day.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵירַב בְּפַת בָּרִאשׁוֹן מְעָרֵב בְּרַגְלָיו בַּשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב יהודה's list of rules from step 4 by adding the two 'switching' cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread to feet is permitted. Feet to bread is forbidden, because one may not begin a bread עירוב on a holy day for the next day.

steps.title: שמואל: Continuing a bread עירוב requires the same bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב יהודה's rule that bread on the first day allows bread on the second. שמואל adds that it must be the same bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the rule 'If he made an עירוב with bread for the first day, he makes it with bread for the second day', שמואל said: and only with that same bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks out one of רב יהודה's rules and records שמואל's limit on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the same bread is just continuing the old עירוב, so it is not a new act of preparation. Using a new loaf would count as starting a fresh bread עירוב on a holy day, which step 5 just forbade.

keyTerms.meaning: And with that same bread

steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to step 5. Only continuing an existing bread עירוב is allowed, not starting a new one.

phrases.english: If he made an eruv with bread on the first day,
he makes an eruv with bread on the second day —
Shmuel said: and with that same bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows one of רב יהודה's rules from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bread עירוב for the second day is valid only if it uses the same bread as the first day.

steps.title: רב אשי shows the משנה's wording supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that the משנה describes taking the same עירוב home after the first day and bringing it back for the second day. This fits שמואל's 'same bread' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is exact in a way that supports this too, because it teaches: How does he do it? He brings the עירוב there before the first day, waits with it until dark, then takes it and goes home. Before the second day he waits with it until dark again, then eats it and goes home.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for שמואל from the exact wording of a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes one piece of food doing the job for both days. He takes it away after the first night and brings the same one back. If any bread would do, why should the משנה bother with this? The detail suggests the same bread is required.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise: the wording also supports this
He waits with it until nightfall

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The mishna's wording is also precise this way,
as it teaches: What does he do?
He brings it there before the first day and stays with it until dark,
then takes it and goes home.
Before the second day, he stays with it until dark,
then eats it and goes home.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that the second day's bread עירוב must be the same bread
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's step-by-step process, in which the same food is taken home after the first day and returned for the second

steps.title: Other רבנן: The משנה is only giving good advice
steps.stepSummary: Other רבנן reject רב אשי's proof. They say the משנה may only be offering practical advice about how one עירוב can cover both days, not a requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן who disagree with שמואל would say: Maybe there, the משנה is just teaching us good advice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how those who disagree with שמואל would push back on רב אשי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's method is a smart, easy way to manage, because one piece of food covers both days. That does not prove a different loaf would be invalid. So the משנה's wording does not force שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The other Sages, here those who disagree with שמואל
Good advice: a recommendation, not a requirement
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: Bread to feet: allowed. Feet to bread: not allowed. שמואל requires the same bread, and רב אשי supports him from the משנה. Other רבנן say the משנה is only giving advice.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis would say: perhaps there —
it is teaching us good advice.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, דִּילְמָא הָתָם עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's proof from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not necessarily שמואל's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's method may be advice for convenience rather than a legal requirement

steps.title: New משנה: רבי יהודה lets a person set a different עירוב for each day of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: When people feared ראש השנה might last two days, רבי יהודה allows a person to make two עירובין, one for each day. Each day can face a different direction, or one day can have an עירוב while the other has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהודה says: If a person feared that ראש השנה would be extended to two days, he may make two עירובין and say: 'My עירוב for the first day is to the east, and for the second day to the west.' Or: 'For the first day to the west, and for the second day to the east.' Or: 'My עירוב is for the first day, and on the second day I am like the people of my town.' Or: 'My עירוב is for the second day, and on the first day I am like the people of my town.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי יהודה rules that the two possible days of ראש השנה can be handled separately for עירוב purposes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back then, ראש השנה lasted two days only if witnesses to the new moon did not come on the first day. Only one of the two days is truly holy, so רבי יהודה lets each day get its own עירוב plan. 'Like the people of my town' means no special עירוב that day, so he walks only from the town like everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Lest the month be extended, making ראש השנה two days
Like the people of my town: no special עירוב that day

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same as the יום טוב next to שבת case. Here the two days of ראש השנה come from doubt about which day is really holy.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
On Rosh HaShana, if one was afraid
that the month might be extended,
a person may make two eruvin and say:
My eruv for the first day is to the east,
and for the second day to the west.
Or: for the first day to the west, and for the second to the east.
Or: my eruv is for the first day, and on the second I am like the people of my town.
Or: my eruv is for the second day, and on the first I am like the people of my town.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁהָיָה יָרֵא שֶׁמָּא תִּתְעַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a related topic: two days of holiness and עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the two days of ראש השנה may each get a separate עירוב arrangement.

steps.title: The חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים do not accept רבי יהודה's ruling that the two days of ראש השנה can be split for עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by recording that the חכמים reject רבי יהודה's view. This sets up the גמרא's later discussion of why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not allow ראש השנה to be divided into two separately handled days for עירוב. The משנה does not give their reason here. The גמרא identifies whose view this is in step 15, and the reasoning appears in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: And they did not agree with him
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה lets the two days of ראש השנה have separate עירובין. The חכמים disagree.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Records the disagreeing opinion to רבי יהודה's ruling in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים do not permit separate עירובין for the two days of ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a condition on a basket of produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that on the first day of ראש השנה a person may make a condition to separate tithes from a basket of טבל, and then eat it on the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה also said: A person may make a condition about a basket of produce on the first day of the holiday, and eat it on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another ruling of רבי יהודה that is built on the same idea as his עירוב ruling: one of the two days of ראש השנה is surely a regular weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומה and מעשרות is forbidden on יום טוב. So on day one, the person says: 'If today is a weekday, I separate now. If today is יום טוב, I will separate tomorrow.' On day two he repeats the condition the other way around. One of the two separations surely happened on a weekday, so the produce is properly tithed and may be eaten on day two.

keyTerms.meaning: makes a condition
a basket (here, of untithed produce)
produce from which תרומה and tithes have not yet been separated
the first day of the holiday

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda said further:
A person may make a condition about the basket
phrases.notes: A basket of untithed (טבל) produce.

phrases.english: on the first day of the holiday,
phrases.notes: The first day of ראש השנה.

phrases.english: and eat it on the second day.
phrases.notes: One of the two days was surely a weekday, so one separation surely counted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי יהודה's view from step 9 (two separate days on ראש השנה) to tithing produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may make a two-way condition about tithing on the first day of ראש השנה and eat the produce on the second day.

steps.title: An egg laid on the first day, and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that an egg laid on the first day may be eaten on the second day. The חכמים reject both of these rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, an egg that was laid on the first day may be eaten on the second day. And the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives one more example of the same idea, and then the משנה reports that the חכמים do not accept his approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg laid on יום טוב is forbidden that day as נולד, something that only came into being on the holiday. If one of the two days is really a weekday, then either the egg was laid on a weekday, or it is being eaten on a weekday. Either way it is permitted. The חכמים do not accept this logic for ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: an egg that was laid
something newly created on the holiday, forbidden to use that day
they did not agree with him

phrases.english: And similarly, an egg that was laid on the first day,
may be eaten on the second day.
And the Sages did not agree with him.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will soon ask who these חכמים are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to step 11 and records the חכמים's rejection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, an egg laid on day one of ראש השנה is permitted on day two. The חכמים disagree.

steps.title: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס: a conditional prayer wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says the prayer leader on ראש השנה should say 'whether today or tomorrow' on day one and 'whether today or yesterday' on day two. The חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says: The one who leads the prayers on ראש השנה says: 'Strengthen us, ה׳ our God, on this day of the new month, whether it is today or tomorrow.' And on the next day he says: 'Whether it is today or yesterday.' And the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא brings the same idea, that only one of the two days is the real holiday, into the wording of the prayers. Again the חכמים reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא wants the prayer to be honest about the doubt: the real ראש חודש is either today or tomorrow, or on day two, today or yesterday. The חכמים do not want a prayer phrased with a condition. This matches their rejection of רבי יהודה, since they do not treat the two days as 'one real, one weekday.'

keyTerms.meaning: the one who passes before the ark, meaning the prayer leader
strengthen us
whether today or tomorrow
yesterday

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says:
One who passes before the ark
phrases.notes: The שליח ציבור (prayer leader).

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, אוֹמֵר:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel opinion that applies the 'one day is really a weekday' idea to prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי דוסא, the prayer on ראש השנה mentions the doubt about which day is the real one. The חכמים reject this.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with three rulings (basket, egg, prayer) that all treat the two days of ראש השנה as 'one is real, one is a weekday.' Each time, the חכמים disagree.

steps.title: Who are the Sages who disagreed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא is behind the anonymous 'the חכמים did not agree with him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the one who 'did not agree with him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a clarifying question: who exactly are these unnamed חכמים? This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack. The גמרא wants to identify the view behind the anonymous חכמים, because that tells us how the opinions line up.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
who?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on this משנה.

phrases.english: Who are those who "did not agree with him"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the identity of the חכמים who rejected רבי יהודה's two-עירובין ruling in step 10. רב's answer and the ברייתא in steps 15-16 deal specifically with the עירוב case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion is represented by the anonymous חכמים who disagreed with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב: it is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the dissenting חכמים follow the opinion of רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב identifies the unnamed חכמים as following רבי יוסי. The next step brings a ברייתא to show where רבי יוסי says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By naming רבי יוסי, רב tells us that the חכמים's view is really one specific תנא's position. It is not necessarily the majority view.

phrases.english: Rav said: It is Rabbi Yosei,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים who disagreed with רבי יהודה hold like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The ברייתא: most Sages allow two עירובין on ראש השנה, but רבי יוסי forbids
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר that on ראש השנה a person may make two עירובין, one for each day, but רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: The חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר that on ראש השנה, when a person feared the month might be extended, he may make two עירובין. He says: 'My עירוב on the first day is to the east, and on the second to the west.' Or: 'On the first to the west, and on the second to the east.' Or: 'My עירוב is for the first day, and on the second I am like the people of my town.' Or: 'My עירוב is for the second day, and on the first I am like the people of my town.' רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב. It shows that רבי יוסי is the one who does not split the two days of ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the majority allows treating each day separately for עירוב, in any of four ways. Only רבי יוסי forbids this, because he does not split the two days. So the 'חכמים' in our משנה who rejected רבי יהודה's two-עירובין ruling must hold like רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: lest it (the month) be extended to 30 days
like the people of my town (with no special עירוב)
forbids

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'חכמים' in the משנה does not mean the majority here. According to רב, it is רבי יוסי's view. In the ברייתא, the majority חכמים actually agree to splitting the days. Also note that the ברייתא names רבי אליעזר as the one who allows splitting, even though in our משנה this view is presented by רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the debate over the basket, the egg and the עירוב all comes down to one question: are the two days of ראש השנה two separate days of doubt, or one unit?

phrases.english: As it was taught: The Sages concede to Rabbi Eliezer
regarding Rosh HaShana, that if one was afraid
that the month might be extended,
phrases.notes: That אלול would have 30 days, making ראש השנה fall on the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's answer in step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the dissenting חכמים in the משנה follow רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) in which רבי יוסי alone forbids splitting the two days of ראש השנה for עירוב.
steps.whatToRemember: Making a separate עירוב for each day of ראש השנה is allowed by רבי יהודה (in our משנה), רבי אליעזר, and the majority חכמים in the ברייתא. רבי יוסי forbids it, and according to רב the משנה's dissenting 'חכמים' follow him.

steps.title: רבי יוסי proves the two days of ראש השנה form one holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי challenges the חכמים: you agree that if witnesses come late in the afternoon, both that day and the next are kept holy. So the two days are one holiness and cannot be split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to them: Don't you agree that if witnesses came from מנחה time and onward, we keep that day holy and the next day holy too?!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי explains why he forbids two עירובין. He points to a rule the חכמים already accept and uses it against them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When witnesses came late, the first day had already been kept holy, but it did not become ראש השנה. The next day did. Even so, both days were treated as holy. This shows the two days are not a case of 'one of them is the real day and we are unsure which.' They are one long day with one shared holiness. And if it is one day, you cannot set up one עירוב in one direction for day one and another עירוב in a different direction for day two.

keyTerms.meaning: You agree / concede
Witnesses (here, those who saw the new moon)
From the time of the afternoon offering and onward, meaning late in the day
We conduct ourselves / we observe
Holy; treated as a holy day

steps.confusionAlert: This is still רבי יוסי speaking inside the ברייתא from Step 16. It is not the גמרא asking its own question. The גמרא quoted this ברייתא to show that the חכמים in our משנה follow רבי יוסי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reasoning behind רבי יוסי's position, which according to רב is the view of the משנה's dissenting חכמים. They hold that the two days of ראש השנה are one holiness, so a person cannot make a separate עירוב arrangement for each day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from Step 16 by giving רבי יוסי's reason for forbidding two עירובין
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's position that a person may make two separate עירובין on ראש השנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים already agree that both days are kept holy even when the first day is known not to be ראש השנה. So the days form one unified holiness and cannot be divided into two separate days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two days of ראש השנה are one long holiness, so separate arrangements for each day are not allowed.
